residencyRequirements.description: You or your spouse must have been a Florida resident for at least 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.description: Florida has no mandatory waiting period. Simplified dissolutions can be finalized approximately 30 days after filing.

noFault.name: Marriage Irretrievably Broken
noFault.description: The marriage between the parties is irretrievably broken

fault.name: Mental Incapacity
fault.description: Mental incapacity of one of the parties for a period of 3 years

requirements: Both parties agree the marriage is irretrievably broken
No minor or dependent children and wife is not pregnant
Parties have agreed on division of all assets and liabilities
Both willing to give up right to trial and appeal
Both willing to appear together at clerk's office to sign petition

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Florida Family Law Rules of Procedure

mandatoryDisclosure.rule: Florida Family Law Rules of Procedure 12.285
mandatoryDisclosure.description: Each party must exchange certain information and documents and file a Family Law Financial Affidavit
mandatoryDisclosure.exemption: Simplified dissolution is exempt from mandatory disclosure requirements

legalCitations.description: Equitable distribution of marital assets and liabilities

legalCitations.code: Florida Family Law Rules of Procedure

filingFees.notes: Varies by county. Application for Determination of Civil Indigent Status available for fee waiver.

factors: Standard of living established during the marriage
Age and health of each party

propertyDivision.description: Florida is an equitable distribution state. Marital assets and liabilities are divided fairly but not necessarily equally.
